# Failure policy: no limit ends a run; every condition is reported

Normative model for what may terminate an Agent node, decided 2026-09-27 after the recorded run `chat.e1608e3b0f642edccf7dcb59588deb2a61dbd0fb` died 61 minutes into its work.

## The incident this replaces

That Chat spawned one subagent. The child started background processes whose records landed under the delegating invocation's scope, so the child's own scoped notice and controls could not see them; 49 of them stayed `finished; output not collected`. On the parent's next turn the completion notice enumerated all 49 - one 100-byte line per job around a 391-byte frame, 5291 bytes - and the dispatch precondition on `retryNotice` (4 KiB) rejected the request. The rejection was classified as a context-preparation failure, so the Agent node failed with `context preparation failed: Invalid model context: provider failed: provider tool request is invalid` and the run stopped with `outcome_uncertain`. The model, the tools and the task were all healthy.

## Invariants

1. Exactly three classes of condition terminate an Agent node: the model's final answer; user cancellation; and an unrecoverable refusal. An unrecoverable refusal is only the trusted core refusing to durably record an exchange, or a provider that accepts a turn and returns neither an answer nor a tool call. Nothing else qualifies.
2. Every other condition - provider, transport, contract, context preparation, tool invocation, tool settlement, budget, counter, deadline or limit - is reported to the model as a bounded notice and the loop continues.
3. A bound sizes the notice, never the run. Truncation is explicit: the notice states what it omitted and how to retrieve it (for jobs, `job_list`).
4. Counters, budgets and token totals are telemetry. None is a termination control; there is no total model-turn, tool-call, recovery or notice cap. A repeated condition keeps being reported as a repeat reminder.
5. Structural validation has two roles and two outcomes. An editor may reject a document and explain why; dispatch must degrade - bound, truncate or drop the advisory field - because a rejected dispatch is a dead run.
6. Reporting is durable. A reported condition is committed as an event, so a restart resumes on the same notice the model last saw instead of replaying the original failure.

## Consequences, accepted deliberately

A provider that never recovers no longer ends the run: the model keeps being told at a bounded rate, and the user's stop is the exit. A job inventory of any size is summarized, not enumerated. A context that cannot be projected under the current tool selection is declined and the pass continues on its own context.

## Evidence

`desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/tool_loop/jobs/registry.rs` bounds the notice with an omitted count. `desktop/src-tauri/src/runtime/model_tool_loop.rs` and the text-only loop in `graph_pass.rs` route every condition through the report path; a tool that cannot settle becomes an error result the model reads. Regression tests pin a 1000-job notice, a 64 KiB notice, a repeated provider failure, a context-preparation condition and a failed tool call as non-terminating.

## Non-responsibilities

This policy does not decide what a notice says, how compaction reduces a context, or which provider response counts as empty. Bounded notice content belongs to the producer; the termination set belongs here.
